title: VelaHealth infosec workshop artifact bundle and response notes
content:
Purpose:
This working doc summarizes answers we drafted in the 2025-10-01 workshop with VelaHealth, lists the evidentiary artifacts we can share, records workshop decisions, and tracks open engineering/legal validation items. Intended as internal bundle to assemble the customer-facing evidence packet after NDA.

Customer context:
- Customer: VelaHealth (HIPAA-regulated healthcare SaaS)
- Engagement: Solutions engineering POC + security questionnaire review for dedicated/private deployment options
- Workshop date: 2025-10-01 (onsite)
- Redwood attendees: Asha (owner), Liam (solutions), Maya (platform eng)

What we're providing in this bundle (high level):
- Draft answers to VelaHealth questionnaire sections (encryption, keys, identity, logging, vulnerability mgmt, incident response, backups, residency).
- Index of shareable artifacts (links and where they live).
- Workshop notes, decisions, open questions and action items with owners + proposed due dates.

Artifact index (can be shared after NDA / per-customer redaction as needed):
1) runtime-encryption-kms-overview.pdf  — diagram and short notes on KMS integration and customer-managed key flow (drive link available)
2) onboarding-playbook-velahealth.pdf  — Dedicated/Private onboarding checklist and network hardening checklist
3) audit-logs-sample-7days.csv  — sanitized audit log export (no PHI). Will provide via secure share.
4) s3-data-encryption-config.txt  — example Terraform snippet for S3 server-side encryption and bucket policy (GitHub PR 572)
5) vulnerability-scan-results-2025-09-30.pdf  — internal vuln-scan report (redacted)
6) incident-response-runbook-v2.md  — IR runbook and notification templates (Confluence: CONFLUENCE-SEC-1023)
7) background-checks-and-roles.csv  — redacted staffing/role matrix for personnel access control
8) private-deploy-network-arch.png  — VPC peering + optional no-internet egress architecture (engineering drive)
9) SOC2-summary-2024.pdf  — redacted SOC 2 Type II summary and coverage window
10) backup-snapshot-encryption-policy.txt — notes on snapshot encryption, retention, and restore process (internal)

Draft questionnaire responses (high-level, for transfer into customer packet):
Encryption at rest:
- All customer data at rest is encrypted using AES-256. For Hosted/Dedicated deployments we use provider-managed disk encryption plus application-level envelope encryption. For Private deployments customers may supply their own CMKs (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, or HSM). See artifact: runtime-encryption-kms-overview.pdf and s3-data-encryption-config.txt.

Encryption in transit:
- Control plane and data plane traffic use TLS 1.2+ with modern cipher suites. Mutual TLS is available for Private deployments and for customers requesting client cert auth.

Key management:
- Redwood supports both Redwood-managed and customer-managed keys. Customer-managed keys integrate directly with the customer's KMS; HSM-backed key usage is supported for Private packages. Key rotations are supported; engineering to validate rotation behavior for in-memory caches (open item).

Identity and access control:
- RBAC enforced across control plane. Enterprise customers use SSO (OIDC/SAML) with SCIM provisioning. Admin actions and token issuance are recorded in audit logs. Private deployments can federate with customer IdP.

Logging and monitoring:
- Audit logs (control plane and user-level events) are retained by default for 90 days; configurable. We provide sanitized sample logs: audit-logs-sample-7days.csv. Prometheus-compatible metrics and tracing endpoints are exposed in Private/Dedicated deployments.

Incident response:
- We maintain an IR runbook and notification templates. For Sev-1 incidents initial acknowledgement target is 1 hour. Full IR runbook: incident-response-runbook-v2.md.

Vulnerability management:
- Weekly automated scans, with triage SLAs for critical/high findings. External pen tests performed quarterly or on major releases. Artifact: vulnerability-scan-results-2025-09-30.pdf.

Third-party assurance and audits:
- Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II coverage (summary in SOC2-summary-2024.pdf). Additional audit evidence can be provided under NDA.

Data residency and multi-tenancy:
- Customers choose region for Hosted/Dedicated. Private deployments run wholly inside customer network/VPC for zero cross-tenant co-location. Tenant isolation via process/container separation and per-tenant storage.

Backups and snapshots:
- Snapshots are encrypted using the same KMS configuration as customer data; default retention policies documented in backup-snapshot-encryption-policy.txt. Engineering to confirm snapshot rotation and restore process for Dedicated/Private (open item).

On-prem / air-gapped options:
- We offer an air-gapped Private package: control plane can run in-customer, updates via offline bundles, and all secrets can remain on-prem. See private-deploy-network-arch.png for network patterns.

Legal/compliance notes:
- We provide a DPA and can execute a BAA for HIPAA customers. Legal to supply standard BAA when requested.

Workshop notes (2025-10-01) summary:
- VelaHealth attendees: Claire Y. (security), Sam R. (infra)
- Redwood attendees: Asha, Liam, Maya
- Primary customer asks:
  1) Show key custody controls and CMK rotation flow with minimal service impact
  2) Provide sanitized audit log samples with no PHI
  3) Deliver architecture diagram for Private deployment with no internet egress
  4) Clarify backup/snapshot encryption and retention policy

Key workshop decisions:
- Provide redacted audit logs and Private network diagram.
- Schedule KMS deep-dive with VelaHealth security team (follow-up meeting).

Open questions / action items:
- KMS rotation behavior for in-memory caches (can rotation happen without full rolling restarts?). Owner: platform-eng (Maya). Target: 2025-10-10.
- Confirm default snapshot encryption and restore process for Dedicated/Private. Owner: infra (Liam). Target: 2025-10-08.
- Produce sanitized audit log export (no PHI) and prepare secure transfer. Owner: security (Asha). Target: 2025-10-07.
- Legal: review and confirm BAA template applicability to Private on-prem package. Owner: Legal. Target: 2025-10-12.

Planned next steps:
1) Assemble artifact bundle (items 1–10) and share via secure file transfer once NDA in place. Owner: Asha.
2) KMS integration deep-dive with VelaHealth security (schedule: 2025-10-15). Owner: Maya.
3) Engineering to prepare a short technical memo on rotation impact to caches and restore procedures. Owner: Liam/Maya.
4) Log sanitization runbook to be created and validated. Owner: Asha.
5) Track all asks in JIRA-POC-487.

Draft customer-facing blurb to include in packet:
"Redwood supports customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private deployments. Our KMS integration preserves auditability while enabling customers to control key lifecycle; we will work with VelaHealth to provide a redacted audit sample and a Private-deploy network diagram for review."

Version history (in-document):
- 2025-10-03: initial draft after workshop (Asha)
- 2025-10-07: added artifact list and log sanitization plan (Asha)
- 2025-10-20: engineering notes added on rotation behavior (Maya)
- 2025-11-12: consolidated artifacts and updated SOC2 reference (Liam)

If you want this as a machine-readable manifest (CSV or Sheet) I can export the artifact index and action items into a separate sheet.
